To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
medications are effective in the treatment of BPD, and that the effectiveness of medications varies according to the symptoms being treated.

1) mood stabilizers are effective for the reduction of impulsivity and affective dysregulation, 2) antipsychotics have not been shown to reduce anger and aggression, 3) antidepressants have not been shown in general to reduce impulsivity or anger, but may be effective in reducing anger and aggression if the patient is also depressed, and 4) anticonvulsants are effective in reducing anger if the anger is comorbid with depression.

(i) mood stabilizers and second-generation antipsychotics may be effective in treating the core features of borderline personality disorder, but (ii) the evidence for their effectiveness is not strong enough to warrant their use as first-line treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the most effective medications and their combinations for the treatment of BPD.
the development of a novel approach to the treatment of borderline patients with the help of medication.

the development of novel, noninvasive and nonpharmacologic therapies for the treatment of psychiatric disorders, such as depression, schizophrenia, anxiety disorders and borderline personality disorder (BPD).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is insufficient evidence to recommend medications for the treatment for borderline personality disorder.
the effectiveness of medications for borderline personality disorder has not been proven in randomized controlled trials.
medications have a role in the management of borderline personality disorder, but more studies are needed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
medications are not a panacea but can be helpful adjuncts in treating the symptoms of borderline personality disorder.
medications can be helpful in the treatment of patients with borderline personality disorder.
the medications are effective adjuncts to psychotherapies, especially in the treatment of comorbid depression, anger, and anxiety.
The main takeaway from our work is that
medications are effective in treating symptoms of borderline personality disorder when combined with psychotherapy.
there is a lack of research on medications in the treatment of BPD.
the use of mood stabilizers, particularly valproate, and antipsychotic medications are the most promising medications to use in the treatment of BPD.
